ticket.text: an account id above the 64-bit range gives a server error.

acceptanceCriteria.text: for the id 9223372036854775808, (1) GET /api/accounts/{id} gives 404; (2) GET /api/accounts/{id}/statement gives 404; (3) POST /api/transfers with that value as from_account_id gives 404 and moves no money.

ticket.text: a maximum length for the statement window.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a window has at most 366 days, with the from date and the to date counted; a window of 366 days is accepted; a window of 367 days or more gives 400.

ticket.text: spaces around a transfer reference are stored.

acceptanceCriteria.text: (1) the reference is stored without spaces at its start and its end; (2) a reference that has only spaces is stored as no reference (null in the statement).

ticket.text: customers type the destination account number in different forms and the transfer is refused.

acceptanceCriteria.text: each of these forms finds the account YMS-0000-0003: (1) lower case, yms-0000-0003; (2) spaces at the start and the end; (3) spaces in place of the hyphens, YMS 0000 0003.

ticket.text: disable the interactive API pages.

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /docs, GET /redoc and GET /openapi.json each return 404; the web page at / still returns 200.

ticket.text: a statement line tells the other account of a transfer.

acceptanceCriteria.text: each statement line has counterparty_number; for a transfer it is the number of the other account of the transfer (the destination on a line with a negative amount, the source on a line with a positive amount); for a deposit and a withdrawal it is null.

ticket.text: A large transfer must have a reference. Without one, the API gives 422.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A large transfer must have a reference. Without one, the API gives 422.

ticket.text: the invariant check finds a journal entry with no lines.

acceptanceCriteria.text: ledger.check_invariants returns the problem entry {id} has no lines for each row of journal_entries that has no row in journal_lines; consistent books still give an empty list.

ticket.text: the insufficient-funds reply tells what is available.

acceptanceCriteria.text: when a transfer is refused for insufficient funds, the response has the status 409 (as before) and detail is an object with message and available_minor, the balance of the source account.

ticket.text: move the default statement window out of the HTTP handler.

acceptanceCriteria.text: (1) the new function ledger.statement_window(start, end, today) returns the pair of dates that the handler used before: a missing end is today, and a missing start is 29 days before the end; (2) api.read_statement calls it; (3) the behaviour of the statement endpoint does not change.

ticket.text: a display text for amounts.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the text has the decimals of the currency and a comma between each group of three digits of the whole part (1,234.50 for 123450 EUR; 1,234,567 for 1234567 JPY; 1,234.567 for 1234567 BHD); for a negative amount the minus sign is first and the digits are grouped the same way (-123.45 for -12345 EUR; -1,234.56 for -123456 EUR).

ticket.text: an amount with decimals that are all zero is refused.

acceptanceCriteria.text: an amount is accepted if each decimal after the decimals of the currency is zero ("1.0" in JPY is 1 minor unit; "1.2300" in EUR is 123 minor units; "10.000" in a transfer between two EUR accounts gives 201 and the amount "10.00"); an amount with a decimal that is not zero after the decimals of the currency is still refused.

ticket.text: the date on which an account was opened.

acceptanceCriteria.text: each account object of the API (GET /api/accounts and GET /api/accounts/{id}) has opened_on, the UTC date of the creation of the account in the form YYYY-MM-DD.

ticket.text: support staff can read a statement.

acceptanceCriteria.text: (1) a request for GET /api/accounts/{id}/statement with the header X-Support-Token equal to the environment variable BANK_SUPPORT_TOKEN gets the statement of any customer account, with no session; (2) with a wrong header or no header, the behaviour is the same as before (401 with no session, 404 for an account of a different customer); (3) if BANK_SUPPORT_TOKEN is not set or is empty, no token is accepted.

ticket.text: the session tells what the customer has.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the body of GET /api/session has (1) account_count, the number of accounts of the customer, and (2) currencies, the list of the different currency codes of those accounts, in the order of the code.

ticket.text: a share of an amount, for later use by interest and fees.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the result is amount * basis_points / 10000 in the currency of the amount, rounded to the minor unit with the rule "half to even" (the rule that to_minor uses); a negative basis_points raises ValueError.

ticket.text: a session cookie with a very long number gives a server error.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a request with the cookie yms_customer set to a text of 30 digits gets 401, the same as each other unknown session.

ticket.text: old idempotency keys are not removed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: each call of ledger.transfer_once deletes all keys of that customer that are older than 24 hours; a key that is exactly 24 hours old, or newer, stays.

ticket.text: the transfer response tells if the money stays with the customer.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the body of POST /api/transfers has internal: true if the destination account belongs to the customer of the session, false if not; a replay (the same Idempotency-Key) has the same value as the first response.

ticket.text: the account number has a wrong form for a very large sequence number (account_number(100000000) gives YMS-10000-0000).

acceptanceCriteria.text: (1) ledger.account_number raises LedgerError for a sequence below 1 or above 99,999,999; (2) for each sequence from 1 to 99,999,999 the number is the same as before.

ticket.text: a clear message for an unknown destination.

acceptanceCriteria.text: (1) a transfer to an account number that does not exist gives 404 with the detail destination account not found; (2) a transfer to an account that exists but cannot receive the transfer (a different currency, or a system account) gives the same status and the same body as (1), so that the reply does not tell that the account exists.

ticket.text: a statement with an early to date and no from date shows a start date before the supported range.

acceptanceCriteria.text: if from is not given, the default start date is not before 1900-01-01; for to=1900-01-05 the body has "from": "1900-01-01"; for a to date of 1900-01-30 or later the default start does not change.

ticket.text: the total of the customer in each currency.

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /api/balances returns, for the customer of the session, a list of {"currency", "total_minor", "total"} in the order of the currency code; total_minor is the sum of the balances of the accounts of that customer in that currency.

ticket.text: the statement page shows only the date of a posting, so two postings of one day cannot be told apart.

acceptanceCriteria.text: each row of the statement table on the web page shows the date and the time of the posting in the form YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (UTC).
